**Order filled:** Buy 44 AAPL @ limit $222.75 (filled at $222.75) — total ≈ $9,801, within the $10,000/order and $20,000/day caps, funded from the $50,000 cash balance (no money left the account).

**Summary of what I did and why:** I read Apple's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01, year ended 2024-09-28), checked the latest news, and pulled a live quote before acting. The 10-K shows total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), gross margin of $180.7 billion (46.2% vs 44.1%), and operating income of $123.2 billion (up from $114.3 billion) — but **net income of $93,736 million for fiscal 2024 versus $96,995 million for fiscal 2023**, a ~3.4% decline despite higher revenue and record operating profit, because the effective tax rate jumped to 24.1% from 14.7% on a one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge tied to the European Commission's State Aid Decision (Ireland). In other words, the earnings dip is a tax/legal item, not operating deterioration: operating cash flow rose to $118.3 billion from $110.5 billion, Services grew 13% to $96.2 billion, and the company returned $95.0 billion via buybacks plus $15.2 billion of dividends. News flow was neutral-to-constructive — Q4 revenue of $94.9 billion (+6% y/y), steady iPhone 16 supplier builds into December, Apple Intelligence rolling out, and analysts leaving holiday-quarter estimates unchanged, with the stock "little changed" around $222. With the shares trading at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order at $222.75 — essentially at the ask, i.e., close to market as the mandate requires — for 44 shares (~$9,801), keeping the position size under the per-order cap and leaving the rest of the daily budget and cash untouched.
